content: When diagnosing diabetes in the absence of classic symptoms, it is recommended to obtain two abnormal test results. These results can either come from the same test or from two different types of tests. If the results from two different tests are inconsistent, the higher value should be repeated to confirm the diagnosis. For example, if the hemoglobin A1c level is 6.5% (48 mmol/mol) or higher, but the fasting plasma glucose (FPG) level is below the diagnostic threshold, healthcare providers should still consider the possibility of diabetes. In such cases, close monitoring of the patient is advised to ensure accurate diagnosis and appropriate management.
